summary: The audit checks 135 units, BIOS 217 and one graduate statistics course of 3 or more units, and NEPR 399, each required course letter graded at B or better. PhD students take the NEPR core courses with nine quarters of NEPR 280 and three quarters of NEPR 299 rotations; MSTP students instead take NEPR 209, 211, 212 and 288, one of NEPR 201, 203, 207 or 208, NEPR 202 or 204, and three quarters of NEPR 280 (two of them for 2 units), with no rotations. Checked by hand: the pre-approved advanced courses (six units with one course of 3 or more, or one 3-unit course for MSTP students), the SIN Boot Camp, the neuroanatomy sessions (not for MSTP students), a first-author paper, the qualifying exam, the oral exam and the dissertation.

ZG3Lsc2N.why: "Required courses must be taken for a letter grade and passed with a 3.0 (B) or better. MSTP students will take NEPR 209, NEPR 211, NEPR 212, and NEPR 288. MSTP students will take one of NEPR 201, NEPR 203, NEPR 207, or NEPR 208. MSTP students will also take either NEPR 202 or NEPR 204." "Students must complete special sessions in neuroanatomy. (Not required for MSTP students.)" "9 quarters of NEPR 280 (Journal Club) are required. MSTP students in the Neurosciences PhD program are required to take 3 quarters of Journal Club and at least 2 quarters must be taken for 2 units." Advanced Courses: "Six units of advanced neuroscience coursework are required. To complete the six units, at least one course must be three units or more" and "One course of 3 units of advanced neuroscience coursework are required for MSTP students." Rotations: "Students rotate through at least three labs during the first year, enrolling in NEPR 299 each quarter ... MSTP students are exempt from this requirement". So the core, Journal Club, advanced courses, rotations and neuroanatomy differ for MSTP students; NEPR 280 and NEPR 299 are repeatable.
